# Sources {#sec-sources}

The chapters link out at the point of use. This is the same shelf, grouped
so you can see what kind of document each one is. Manuals beat blog posts.
Source beats manuals when they disagree. Papers beat this book's readings
of the papers.

## The runtime, primary

- [R Internals](https://cran.r-project.org/doc/manuals/r-release/R-ints.html),
  for R 4.6.1 (2026-06-24). SEXPTYPEs, the header, allocation classes,
  environments, attributes, special primitives, the character cache. The
  manual warns that it is a work in progress. Believe it, and check the
  source when a sentence is load-bearing.
- [The R Language Definition](https://cran.r-project.org/doc/manuals/r-release/R-lang.html).
  The C-syntax / Lisp-and-APL-semantics paragraph, and the chapter on
  computing on the language.
- [`src/main/memory.c`](https://github.com/wch/r-source/blob/trunk/src/main/memory.c)
  in the `wch/r-source` mirror. Nil's initialization, node classes, the
  generational heap. The comment "or armageddon happens" is not a joke you
  need to improve on.
- [`src/include/Defn.h`](https://github.com/wch/r-source/blob/trunk/src/include/Defn.h).
  `REFCNTMAX`, `MARK_NOT_MUTABLE`, the increment and decrement macros that
  refuse to move a saturated count.
- Luke Tierney,
  [Notes on Reference Counting in R](https://developer.r-project.org/Refcnt.html).
  The design note from when reference counting was still opt-in. Read it
  for motivation and for the list of holders that deliberately do not
  count. Do not read it as a description of the compile flags in a current
  release. Current dumps print `REF(n)` because the switch happened.
- Luke Tierney, Gabe Becker, and Tomas Kalibera,
  [ALTREP: Alternative Representations for R Objects](https://svn.r-project.org/R/branches/ALTREP/ALTREP.html).
  The design note. The 2017 DSC slides circulate as
  [a PDF](https://www.r-project.org/dsc/2017/slides/dsc2017.pdf); the tech-doc
  index is
  [developer.r-project.org/TechDocs](https://developer.r-project.org/TechDocs/).

## The language, primary

- John M. Chambers,
  [S, R, and Data Science](https://journal.r-project.org/articles/RJ-2020-028/),
  *The R Journal* 12/1 (2020). The three principles, in his wording, with
  the 1976 blackboard and the reason there are no scalars. The book he
  points at is *Extending R* (Chapman and Hall/CRC, 2016), pages 4--11.
- Ross Ihaka and Robert Gentleman,
  [R: A Language for Data Analysis and Graphics](https://doi.org/10.1080/10618600.1996.10474713),
  *Journal of Computational and Graphical Statistics* 5/3 (1996).
- Floréal Morandat, Brandon Hill, Leo Osvald, and Jan Vitek,
  [Evaluating the Design of the R Language](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-642-31057-7_6),
  ECOOP 2012.
- Hadley Wickham, [*Advanced R*](https://adv-r.hadley.nz/), 2nd ed., 2019.
  In particular
  [names and values](https://adv-r.hadley.nz/names-values.html),
  [environments](https://adv-r.hadley.nz/environments.html),
  [object systems](https://adv-r.hadley.nz/oo.html),
  and [conditions](https://adv-r.hadley.nz/conditions.html).
- Hadley Wickham,
  [A Layered Grammar of Graphics](https://doi.org/10.1198/jcgs.2009.07098),
  *Journal of Computational and Graphical Statistics* 19/1 (2010).
  Wilkinson's *Grammar of Graphics* (Springer, 2005) is the prior
  vocabulary.
- [httr2](https://httr2.r-lib.org/articles/httr2.html),
  [ellmer](https://ellmer.tidyverse.org/),
  [cli](https://cli.r-lib.org/),
  and [rlang::try_fetch()](https://rlang.r-lib.org/reference/try_fetch.html).
- The companion design manual:
  [S7 Design Notes](https://docs.jimbrig.com/s7-design-notes/).

## Conditions, types, and shells

- Kent M. Pitman,
  [Condition Handling in the Lisp Language Family](https://nhplace.com/kent/Papers/Condition-Handling-2001.html)
  (2001). The Common Lisp mechanism itself is
  [HyperSpec chapter 9](http://www.lispworks.com/documentation/HyperSpec/Body/09_.htm).
- Alexis King,
  [Parse, don't validate](https://lexi-lambda.github.io/blog/2019/11/05/parse-don-t-validate/)
  (2019).
- John Launchbury and Simon Peyton Jones, "Lazy Functional State Threads,"
  POPL 1994. The paper behind `runST`.
  [Microsoft Research hosts the publication](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/publication/lazy-functional-state-threads/).
- Gary Bernhardt,
  [Boundaries](https://www.destroyallsoftware.com/talks/boundaries).
  Functional core, imperative shell. The talk is the source of the phrase
  as used here.
- Eric Evans, *Domain-Driven Design* (Addison-Wesley, 2003). Ubiquitous
  language. The enterprise apparatus is optional; the vocabulary is not.
- [The Rust book, chapter on traits](https://doc.rust-lang.org/book/ch10-02-traits.html)
  and the [Rust API guidelines](https://rust-lang.github.io/api-guidelines/).
  Read these before repeating the "R is just like Rust" line to someone
  who writes Rust. The shared posture is open operations over types. The
  ownership story does not transfer.

## PowerShell and the view layer

- Jeffrey P. Snover, the Monad manifesto, 8 August 2002.
  [Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/scripting/developer/monad-manifesto)
  hosts it;
  [the PDF](https://jsnover.com/Docs/MonadManifesto.pdf)
  is the text. "Instead of piping unstructured text, we pipe .NET objects."
- [about_Output_Streams](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/microsoft.powershell.core/about/about_output_streams)
  and
  [about_Redirection](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/microsoft.powershell.core/about/about_redirection).
  Stream numbers. See the [open question](open-questions.qmd) on the
  version-introduced discrepancy before you cite a year.
- [about_Format.ps1xml](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/microsoft.powershell.core/about/about_format.ps1xml).
  Views affect display only. Built-in views moved into source in
  PowerShell 6. The separation is the idea; the XML is the aged vehicle.

## What not to cite this book for

Do not cite it for a guarantee about a future R, or for S7 behavior past
what the S7 design notes have rechecked. Do not cite the Cairo / WinFS
paragraph as a history of .NET; it is a warning against a bad history.
Do not cite a `REF` count from an IDE session as a property of an
expression. Cite the manuals, the source, and the probes in
`verification/` for anything that has to survive contact with a different
machine.
